review.headline: Missed tactical shots resolved by a decisive late rook fork

sections.text: Out of a solid Queen's Gambit Declined, you broke the center with 10...e5. White slipped immediately with 11.e4?, allowing you to strike with 11...exd4!, grabbing a central pawn and opening lines for your pieces.

The game grew sharper after your kingside expansion with 14...g5?! and 15...Bg7?. You ran into trouble on move 17: under pressure, 17...Qc7? pinned your own knight along the c7-g3 diagonal, when simply trading off their attacker was better. White let you off the hook with 18.Nxe4? instead of invading with the knight, allowing you to trade down pieces.

After trading queens with 21...Qe6! and 22...Rxe6, White made passive pawn pushes on the queenside. Both 24.b3?? and 25.a4?? left the e1-rook unprotected on the open file, giving you the chance for an immediate knockout. You missed it with 24...Bg7?? and 25...f5??, but when White erred again with 27.Bxf4??, you finally unleashed 27...Nf3+!. This move delivered a fork against the king and rook while creating a discovered attack down the e-file, winning the exchange on e1.

review.turning_point: White's 27.Bxf4?? allowed 27...Nf3+!, where the knight fork and discovered attack down the open e-file won decisive material.
review.focus: Look for discovered attacks along open files when an opponent leaves a major piece undefended, such as the missed 24...Nf3+.
